messages:
mike-h: Heads up — us-west1 GPU pools are at ~94% utilization and we're seeing a long tail of queued requests. FIFO is keeping latency tight for small requests but large background batching jobs are piling up and starving the pool.
anya: ugh. can you paste the queue depth graph? are these mostly long-context requests or big batches?
mike-h: mostly long-context (32k) and a handful of heavy embedding batches. queue depth spike aligns with a nightly retrain push from one customer.
raj-p: this is the classic backpressure problem. FIFO favors short latency but not throughput fairness. we should consider a hybrid: per-route limits + priority buckets.
devon: agreed. thought: windowed priority queuing — allocate capacity windows per priority class every 5s to guarantee forward progress for low-prio batch jobs.
lina-w: how would that interact with autoscale? if we reserve capacity for low-prio we might waste GPUs during low load.
anya: maybe use soft reservations: a token-bucket per-priority that refills based on realtime capacity, not fixed GPUs. if pool saturates tokens get throttled.
mike-h: example config sketch:
```yaml
admission:
  windows:
    - name: realtime
      weight: 70
      token_rate: 1400ms
    - name: batch
      weight: 30
      token_rate: 6000ms
  preemption: true # allow realtime to borrow if idle, but return to batch otherwise
  max_inflight_per_route: 15
```
raj-p: i like token-based windows + per-route caps. also need a penalty for misbehaving tenants (heavy retries). maybe exponential backoff + temporary route dampening.
devon: another axis is drop-before-queue for huge requests: if estimated token cost > threshold, reject with 429+Retry-After rather than occupy a slot.
lina-w: for fairness metrics, we should emit per-priority tail latency and token-usage rate. dashboards + alerts when batch waiting > 3x normal.
sre-bot: alert: GPU-pool-us-west1-queue-depth exceeded 80 for 12min — trigger: oncall-eng-infra
anya: can we test this in canary? propose feature flag that enables windowed-priority on 10% of traffic in us-west1 during off-peak.
raj-p: yep. test plan:
- deploy token-bucket admission
- enable for internal routes + 10% customer traffic
- run synthetic long-context + large batch mix
- measure p95/p99 latency for realtime and average wait time for batch
mike-h: agree. add a safety fallback: if tokens exhausted and overall queue growth rate > 20%/min, automatically switch to region-level shed (reject lowest priority).
lina-w: cost note: if we start rejecting large batches, some customers will shift to Dedicated. we should flag high-cost-on-rejection in billing metadata so sales can follow up.
devon: also add a quick CLI to tweak weights on the fly:
```
redwoodctl admission set-weight --region us-west1 --priority batch --weight 25
```
anya: cool. i'll draft the canary PR and add the dashboards. mike, can you own the rollout timeline? :thumbsup:
mike-h: will do. planning to roll to canary tomorrow 02:00 UTC. i'll post results here. :rocket:
